top_five.text: Escalating armed conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo trapped an Ebola response team for over 24 hours in Ituri province as an outbreak reaching 11,645 cases and nearly 5,700 deaths severely strains health operations.
Armed gang members killed at least 47 people, including five children, and kidnapped over 50 others in Kenscoff, Haiti, threatening hostageworker massacres if police attempt rescue operations.
Russian missile and drone attacks in Ukraine's Kyiv region killed at least 15 people and destroyed an apartment building in Dymer, leaving at least 11 residents trapped under rubble.

UN agencies reported that 15.9 million people in Afghanistan face acute food insecurity, with over four million children expected to require treatment for acute malnutrition in 2027 amid declining international assistance.

The International Court of Justice ruled that Myanmar's security forces committed genocide against the Rohingya population during a 2017 military crackdown in Rakhine state involving mass killings and village destructions.

top_story.quote: Escalating armed conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo has trapped healthcare workers and severely disrupted medical operations as a major Ebola outbreak reaches 11,645 cases and nearly 5,700 deaths.
top_story.label: AFRICA — DRC Ebola Outbreak and Response Security Crisis

Middle East.headline: Gaza Strip — Airstrikes Target Food Distribution Vehicle and Northern Gaza
Middle East.body: An Israeli airstrike targeted a vehicle carrying food aid in the Tal al-Hawa neighborhood of Gaza City, killing three charity kitchen workers and injuring several others. The attack destroyed the vehicle and scattered meal supplies intended for displaced residents. Separately, an Israeli airstrike in northern Gaza left one person critically injured and several others wounded. The incidents underscore ongoing risks to humanitarian relief workers and civilians seeking food assistance across the Gaza Strip.

Middle East.headline: Yemen — Military Escalation Intensifies as Blockade Worsens Conditions in Taiz
Middle East.body: Clashes between government forces and Houthi fighters have intensified across frontline areas, including Bab al-Mandab, Taiz, and Marib. The Yemeni army reported conducting 816 operations over a 24-hour period, killing or wounding 149 Houthi personnel and damaging or destroying 71 military vehicles. Concurrently, the humanitarian situation in Taiz continues to deteriorate due to an ongoing blockade, soaring commodity prices, and failing public services, compounding hardships for vulnerable populations.
verified_figures: 71 military vehicles and equipment destroyed or damaged

Middle East.headline: Bahrain — Iranian Attack Hits Civilian Industrial Facility, Injuring Civilians
Middle East.body: An Iranian missile and drone attack struck a civilian industrial facility in Bahrain, injuring two people. According to Bahrain's Interior Ministry, a Pakistani resident was critically injured, while a Bahraini citizen sustained stable injuries. Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed the assault targeted U.S. military positions hosting the U.S. Navy's Fifth Fleet. The strike represents a further spillover of regional hostilities triggered by earlier U.S. and Israeli attacks against Iran.

Middle East.headline: Iran / United States — Rising Tensions Over Maritime Blockade and Oil Exports
Middle East.body: Regional tensions have heightened following threats of military action against vessels attempting to bypass blockades affecting Iranian oil exports. Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi declared that Iran will pursue negotiations while maintaining efforts to export oil, emphasizing that the blockade must be broken. Discussions regarding oil exports have gained traction across Iranian national institutions, raising concerns over potential escalation and maritime security risks in the Gulf region.

Americas.headline: Haiti: UN chief condemns Haiti attack that killed 47
Americas.body: At least 47 people, including at least five children, were killed and more than 50 others kidnapped by armed men in Haiti on Sunday, the United Nations confirmed on Tuesday. The incident, which took place in Kenscoff on the outskirts of the capital, Port-au-Prince, is believed to be one of the largest mass kidnappings in the troubled Caribbean country in recent years. In a video posted on social media, a gang leader threatened to murder hostages if Haiti's National Police kill any of his men in an attempt to rescue people. "If any of our soldiers are hurt, I will kill all of them," he said.

Americas.headline: U.S. bans entry from Ebola-affected countries as American patient identified

Americas.headline: Taking Advantage of the Hormuz Blockade... The 'Donroe Doctrine' Makes a Play for Energ...
Americas.body: As crude oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz plunged amid the Iran war, the global oil landscape has been shifting. The Strait of Hormuz was a passageway for one-fifth of the world's crude oil supply, but after shipping was disrupted, pipelines and loading operations in the Red Sea continued to be used. These routes, however, have also been exposed to the risk of attacks by Yemen's pro-Iran armed group, the Houthi rebels. Africa.headline: DRC — Ebola Outbreak Escalates as Fighting Disrupts Response Operations
Africa.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 11,645 cases and nearly 5,700 deaths, remaining the second-largest on record. The World Health Organization announced clinical trials will begin next week for two candidate vaccines targeting the Bundibugyo strain, for which no approved treatment exists. However, escalating fighting in Ituri trapped an Ebola response team and healthcare workers in a hospital maternity ward for over 24 hours. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus called for their safe, immediate evacuation as armed clashes severely disrupt healthcare access and epidemic control efforts near the outbreak's origin.

Africa.headline: Sudan — Drone Strikes Kill Four and Damage UN Facilities in Khartoum
Africa.body: A drone attack targeting Khartoum, Sudan, killed four people and caused damage to United Nations premises. The strike highlights persistent operational hazards and security risks facing international organizations and civilian infrastructure amid ongoing conflict in the capital. Further details regarding the identities of those killed or the exact extent of structural damage to UN facilities were not immediately available.

Africa.headline: South Africa — Femicide Statistics Highlight Severe Protection Concerns
Africa.body: Official statistics published in media reports indicate that 581 women were murdered in South Africa over a three-month period. The high casualty figure underscores severe, ongoing protection concerns and pervasive gender-based violence affecting women across the country.

Europe.headline: Ukraine — Russian strikes kill at least 15 in Kyiv region
Europe.body: Russian missile and drone attacks struck Ukraine's Kyiv region, destroying a five-storey apartment building in the village of Dymer. Ukrainian officials reported at least 15 people were killed in attacks across the region. Search and rescue teams evacuated nine people from the damaged building in Dymer, including a seven-year-old boy rescued after 14 hours under rubble. At least 11 residents are believed to remain trapped under the debris as rescue operations continue.
verified_figures: at least 15 people killed in Kyiv region

Europe.headline: Finland / Baltic Sea — Russia-bound ship targeted in Gulf of Finland
Europe.body: A Russia-bound cargo ship was towed away after being targeted in a drone attack in the Gulf of Finland. According to Finnish defence forces, Ukraine was likely responsible for the strike on the vessel. Ukrainian authorities have not publicly commented on the incident.

Europe.headline: Libya / Russia — Russian warship sinks in Benghazi following suspected drone attack
Europe.body: A Russian naval corvette sank in the port of Benghazi, Libya, following a suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack. According to eastern Libyan officials, the vessel, identified as the Merkury, was docked for refueling and resupply when the strike triggered an explosion. No entity has claimed official responsibility for the attack.

Europe.headline: NATO / Poland — North Atlantic Council convenes over Polish airspace violations
Europe.body: NATO's North Atlantic Council convened a meeting in Brussels to address recent incursions into Polish airspace. The alliance's decision-making body met after prosecutors alleged that at least three Russian missiles violated Poland's airspace during military operations last week.
verified_figures: at least 3 Russian missiles alleged to have violated Polish airspace

Asia-Pacific.headline: Afghanistan — Acute Food Insecurity and Child Malnutrition
Asia-Pacific.body: According to UN agencies including UNICEF, an estimated 15.9 million people in Afghanistan face acute food insecurity, with 3.4 million at emergency hunger levels. Approximately 32 percent of the population experienced Crisis-level or worse hunger between September and October 2026. UNICEF reported that child wasting reached its highest recorded level for the August-October period, and more than four million children are expected to require treatment for acute malnutrition in 2027 amid declining foreign assistance and strained health services.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Myanmar — ICJ Rules Country Responsible for Genocide Against Rohingya
Asia-Pacific.body: The International Court of Justice found Myanmar responsible for committing genocide against the Rohingya population during a 2017 military crackdown in Rakhine state. In a case brought by The Gambia under the Genocide Convention, the court ruled on 19 November that Myanmar's security forces carried out mass killings, widespread sexual violence, and village destructions with intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya group. The verdict highlights ongoing international protection and accountability concerns for millions of displaced Rohingya.

Asia-Pacific.headline: Indonesia — Fatal Confectionery Factory Fire Kills 24 in Banten
Asia-Pacific.body: At least 24 people have been killed and approximately 30 others remain missing after a major fire struck the PT Fonusa Agung Mulia confectionery factory in Cikande, Banten province. Search teams are navigating unstable and damaged structural wreckage to locate missing workers. Authorities are investigating the cause of the blaze, which survivors reported originated in a third-floor cooling unit. At least 15 survivors were rescued alive as emergency operations continued.

Global / Cross-Cutting.headline: DR Congo — Ebola Outbreak Reaches 11,645 Cases Amid Escalating Security Risks for Response Teams
Global / Cross-Cutting.body: An ongoing Ebola epidemic in the Democratic Republic of the Congo has reached 11,645 cases and claimed more than 5,600 lives, remaining a global health emergency. Spreading substantially faster than previous outbreaks, the country's 17th Ebola outbreak surpassed 1,000 confirmed cases within 40 days of response activation. Humanitarian operations face severe security impediments in eastern DR Congo, where fighting around an Ituri province hospital trapped an Ebola response team in a maternity ward for over 24 hours. The World Health Organization has called for the immediate and safe evacuation of the health workers, warning that the clashes have disrupted both hospital operations and the broader regional outbreak response.
